questions.q: Two objects are projected with same velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> however at different angles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math> with the horizontal. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, the ratio of horizontal range of the first object to the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>nd</mi></msup></math> object will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given: α+β=90°

Range of the first projectile:

R1=u2sin2αg

Range of the second projectile:

R2=u2sin2βg=u2sin(180°-2α)g=u2sin2αg

As we can see, both are equal.

R1=R2

Therefore,

R1:R2=1:1

questions.q: When a car is at rest, its driver sees rain drops falling on it vertically. When driving the car with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi></math>, he sees that rain drops coming at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></math> from the horizontal. On further increasing the speed of the car to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">β</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mi></mi></math>, this angle changes to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>45</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">β</mi></math> is close to :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
tan=60°=vrgv               ........1

tan45°=vrg(β+1)v            ..........2

3v=(β+1)v

β=3-1=0.732

If the block takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> to complete one round, the normal force by the side walls of the groove is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
N=mω2R

Given m=0.2 kg,T=40 S,R=0.2 m

Put values in equation 1

N=9.859×10-4 N

questions.q: At time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> a particle starts travelling from a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in a plane keeping <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math> coordinate constant. At any instant of time, it's position along the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> directions are defined as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> respectively. At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> acceleration of the particle will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The position vector of the particle can be written as,

r→=3ti^+5t3j^+7k^

The velocity of the particle will be, 

v→=dr→dt=3i^+15t2j^

Now the acceleration of the particle will be,

a→=dv→dt=d2r→dt2=30tj^

At t=1 s⇒d2rdt2=30j^

questions.q:
The co-ordinates of a particle moving in $x-y$ plane are given by : $x=2+4 \mathrm{t}, y=3 \mathrm{t}+8 \mathrm{t}^2$.
The motion of the particle is :
options: uniformly accelerated having motion along a parabolic path.
uniform motion along a straight line.
uniformly accelerated having motion along a straight line.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & x=2+4 t \\ & \frac{d x}{d t}=v_x=4 \\ & \frac{d v_x}{d t}=a_x=0 \\ & y=3 t+8 t^2 \\ & \frac{d y}{d t}=v_y=3+16 t \\ & \frac{d v_y}{d t}=a_y=16 \end{aligned}$ the motion will be uniformly accelerated motion. For path $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{x}=2+4 \mathrm{t} \\ & \frac{(\mathrm{x}-2)}{4}=\mathrm{t} \end{aligned}$
Put this value of $t$ is equation of $yy=3\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)+8\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)^2$ this is a quadratic equation so path will be parabola.

questions.q: A particle moves such that its position vector <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>ω</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>t</mi><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover></math> where <math><mi>ω</mi></math> is a constant and <math><mi>t</mi></math> is time. Then which of the following statements is true for the velocity <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> and acceleration <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> of the particle:
options: <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is perpendicular to <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is directed away from the origin

<math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is perpendicular to <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is directed towards the origin
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
r→=cos⁡ωti^+sin⁡ωtj^
v→=dr→dt=ω-sin⁡ωti^+cos⁡ωtj^
a→=dv→dt=-ω2cos⁡ωti^+sin⁡ωtj^
a→=-ω2r→∴a→ is antiparallel to r→
v→.r→=ω-sin⁡ωtcos⁡ωt+cos⁡ωtsin⁡ωt=0
So v→⊥r→

questions.q: A river is flowing from west to east direction with speed of $9 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}$. If a boat capable of moving at a maximum speed of $27 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}$ in still water, crosses the river in half a minute, while moving with maximum speed at an angle of $150^{\circ}$ to direction of river flow, then the width of the river is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\therefore \mathrm{V}_{\perp}=$ river flow $=27 \times \cos 60^{\circ}=\frac{27}{2} \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$.
Time taken $=30 \mathrm{sec}$.
$\therefore \mathrm{S}=\mathrm{Vt}=\frac{27}{2} \times \frac{5}{18} \times 30 \mathrm{~m}=112.5 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: A projectile is projected at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> from horizontal with initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The velocity of the projectile at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> from the start will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that v=40 m s-1.

The components of the velocity will be vy=vsin30°=40 m s-12=20 m s-1vx=vcos30°=4032 m s-1=203  m s-1

The time taken to reach maximum height is T=usin30°g=20 m s-110 m s-2=2 s

Hence, at T=2 s, as vy=0 m s-1 therefore vnet=vx=203 m s-1.

questions.q: Motion of a particle in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></math> plane is described by a set of following equations <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The path of the particle will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
x=4sinπ2-ωt=4cosωt,

y=4sinωt

Clearly,   x2+y2=4cosωt2+4sinωt2⇒x2+y2=16

Hence, the path covered by particle is a circle.

questions.q: A butterfly is flying with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in north-east direction. Wind is slowly blowing at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> from north to south. The resultant displacement of the butterfly in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> seconds is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
V→BW=42cos45i^+42sin45j^
=4i^+4j^
V→w=-j^
V→B=V→BW+V→w=4i^+3j^
S→B=V→B×t=(4i^+3j^)×3=12i^+9j^

questions.q: A particle moving in a circle of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> with uniform speed takes time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> to complete one revolution. If this particle is projected with the same speed at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it is equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>R</mi></math>. The angle of projection <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> is then given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of circular motion is given by, 

2πRv=T⇒v=2πRT

Now, maximum height H=v2sin2θ2g

⇒4R=4π2R2T2sin2θ2g

⇒sinθ=2gT2π2R

⇒θ=sin−12gT2π2R12

questions.q: An object moves at a constant speed along a circular path in a horizontal plane with centre at the origin. When the object is at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, its velocity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . The object’s velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and acceleration <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: As the speed is constant, only centripetal acceleration will act(towards the centre of the circular path), ac=v2r=422=8 m s-2 towards the centre which at the given time will be towards right, hence a→c=8i^ m s-2. Velocity of the particle at this instant will in upward direction and hence v→=4j^ m s-1.

questions.q: The stream of a river is flowing with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. A swimmer can swim at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The direction of the swimmer with respect to the flow of the river, to cross the river straight, is

questions.q: A helicopter is flying horizontally with a speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> at an altitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> has to drop a food packet for a man on the ground. What is the distance of helicopter from the man when the food packet is dropped ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The aeroplane imparts v velocity to the food packet horizontally when dropping. Horizontal range of food packet =v×2hg
Also, Horizontal distance, travelled by aeroplane =v×2hg thus, vertical distance between aeroplane and person =h
distance =2v2 h g+h2

questions.q:
If the angular velocity of earth's spin is increased such that the bodies at the equator start floating, the duration of the day would be approximately :
(Take : g=10 ms-2, the radius of earth, R=6400×103 m, Take π=3.14)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For objects to float, 

mg=mω2R

ω= angular velocity of the earth.

R= Radius of earth

ω=gR   ...1

Duration of day =T

T=2πω   ...2

⇒T=2πRg

=2π6400×10310

⇒T60=83.775 minutes

≃84 minutes

questions.q: In a car race on straight road, car A takes a time t less than car B at the finish and passes finishing point with a speed v more than that of car B. Both the cars start from rest and travel with constant acceleration a1 and a2  respectively. Then v is equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, 
Initially both car is at rest, so u1=u2=0
Acceleration of car A & B is a1 & a2

Let us assume,
Time of reach to destination of car A is, t1=t0
Time of reach to destination of car B is, t2=t0+t

Using second equation of motion, we have
u1t+12a1t12=u2t+12a2t22
⇒0×t+12a1t02=0×t+12a2t0+t2
⇒a1a2t0=t0+t
⇒t0=ta1a2-1

From first equation of motion, we have
v1=a1t0 &v2=a2t0+t
⇒v=v1-v2=a1-a2t0-a2t
⇒v=a1-a2ta1a2-1-a2t
⇒v=ta1a2a1-a2-a2a2a1-a2-a2
⇒v=ta1a2-a2a1a1-a2
⇒v=a1.a2 t

questions.q: A child stands on the edge of the cliff <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with an initial speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . Neglecting the air resistance, the speed with which the stone hits the ground will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> (given, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup></math> ).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, u=5 m s-1, h=10 m

Using vy2=uy2+2gh in vertical direction, we have the velocity of stone in vertical direction as vy=2gh=200 m s-1   (since, uy=0).

The final velocity along the horizontal direction is the same as the initial horizontal velocity as there is no acceleration along the x-axis.

The speed with which the stone hits the ground is 

vnet=vx2+vy2=25+200=15 m s-1

questions.q: If the radius of curvature of the path of two particles of same mass are in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn></math>, then in order to have constant centripetal force, their velocities will be in the ratio of:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given m1=m2 and r1r2=34

As centripetal force is given by F=mv2r, in order to have the same centripetal force, we can write

F1=F2⇒m1v12r1=m2v22r2⇒v1v2=r1r2=32

questions.q: The maximum height reached by a projectile is $64 \mathrm{~m}$. If the initial velocity is halved, the new maximum height of the projectile is _____ $\mathrm{m}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{H}_{\max }=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2 \sin ^2 \theta}{2 \mathrm{~g}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{H}_{1 \text { max }}}{\mathrm{H}_{2 \max }}=\frac{\mathrm{u}_1^2}{\mathrm{u}_2^2} \\ & \frac{64}{\mathrm{H}_{2 \max }}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^2}{(\mathrm{u} / 2)^2} \\ & \mathrm{H}_{2 \max }=16 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A swimmer can swim with velocity of 12 km/h in still water. Water flowing in a river has velocity 6 km/h. The direction with respect to the direction of flow of river water he should swim in order to reach the point on the other bank just opposite to his starting point is ________°. 

(Round off to the Nearest Integer) (find the angle in degree)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
12sinθ=vr

sinθ=12

θ=30°

∴ α=120°

questions.q:
A stone tied to 180 cm long string at its end is making 28 revolutions in horizontal circle in every minute. The magnitude of acceleration of stone is 1936x m s-2. The value of x ______.

[Take π=227]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angular velocity, ω=28×2π60 rad s-1.

Required centripetal acceleration is given by,

a=ω2R

=5660×2272×1.8

=(44)2225×1.8=1936125

Hence, required x=125.

questions.q: A fighter jet is flying horizontally at a certain altitude with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. When it passes directly overhead an anti-aircraft gun, a bullet is fired from the gun, at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> with the horizontal, to hit the jet. If the bullet speed is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>°</mo></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In order to hit, horizontal velocity of both moving object should be same,

V1=V2cosθ ⇒200=400cosθ

⇒cosθ=12 ⇒θ=60°

questions.q: A person is swimming with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the flow and reaches to a point directly opposite on the other side of the river. The speed of the flow is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> to the nearest integer is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
10 sin 30°=x
x=5 m/s
